title: Midcycle Capacity Tilt Protocol — dynamic scope reallocation for emergent priority shifts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During the last two cycles we observed that emergent cross-functional work (partner integrations, security patches, and urgent compliance asks) created disproportionate disruption to planned deliverables. Current ad-hoc reassignments increase context switching, elongate lead times, and undermine measurable OKRs. Goal: Define a lightweight, operational protocol (the 'Capacity Tilt') to reallocate people and scope midcycle with clear triggers, guardrails, and a 30-minute decision path. This ticket captures the decision matrix, escalation flow, communication template, and minimal tooling changes required so PMs and Eng leads can safely tilt capacity without breaking rollout commitments.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page decision matrix published in Confluence with example tilt scenarios
A Slack triage workflow (slash command or channel template) that documents the trigger, stakeholders, and timebox
A scoreboard dashboard in Console showing tilt-related commits, scope removed, and on-time delivery delta
Runbook validated in tabletop exercise with at least two cross-functional leads and outcomes captured
Clear post-tilt follow-ups assigned and tracked in Linear within 48 hours
implementation_notes: Define 3 quantitative triggers: customer-severity >= P1, regulatory blocker, or platform outage > 10% SLA degradation
Tilt window is 0-2 weeks into cycle: use immediate triage; 2-4 weeks: require PM + Eng Director sign-off; beyond 4 weeks: executive approval
Scope haircut rules: prefer feature aesthetics > 50% reduction before removing core infra tasks; preserve backward-compatible API contracts
Staffing shadow: identify 1 hot-swap engineer per product team who can absorb 25% load for one week
Guardrails: max two successive tilts per squad per quarter; cap cumulative scope removed to 20% of cycle committed story points

decisions: Keep tilt decision on a 30-minute SLA for the initial triage call; resolution must be recorded in the Slack channel
Classify tilts by window (0-2w fast, 2-4w controlled, >4w exec) with increasing sign-off requirements
Adopt conservative haircut preference: delay removing infra-critical work; prefer deferring non-blocking feature polish
Create a dedicated tilt channel naming convention: #tilt-<cycle>-<short-reason> for auditable discussion

outcomes: Expected: reduce unstructured midcycle scope churn by 40% and shorten decision latency from ~6 hours to <30 minutes for fast-window tilts
Risk: may increase number of small scope skews that require subsequent cross-team coordination; mitigation: cap successive tilts and require OKR sync review
